settings.label: Knowledge Base
title: Knowledge Base
connection.title: GBrain Connection
connection.token.placeholder: Leave empty for the local default
connection.token.hint: Only fill in if your gbrain runs with --auth-token (custom build, remote server, etc.). Our default one-click install runs unauthenticated.
connection.failed: Could not reach gbrain. Is it running?
config.title: Brain settings
config.subtitle: Configure the GBrain instance — connection and runtime status.
config.hint: URL defaults to the local `gbrain serve --http` port (http://127.0.0.1:3131). Override if your server runs on a different port.
config.runtime.title: Runtime
config.runtime.empty: Not connected — runtime info shows up here once GBrain responds.
config.providers.empty: `gbrain providers list` returned nothing. Check that the gbrain CLI is on PATH.
config.providers.envHint: Paste each provider's API key directly here. Values are encrypted via your OS keychain. Saving takes effect immediately — gbrain is restarted in the background.
config.providers.placeholder.saved: saved — paste a new value to replace
stage.stopped.title: Knowledge Base engine not running
stage.stopped.description: GBrain is already installed on this computer but its background service isn't up. This usually happens after a reboot.
stage.stopped.hint: Takes 1-2 seconds. Stays running until you reboot or quit gbrain manually.
stage.noProvider.title: One step away from ready
stage.noProvider.description: The service is up, but you haven't picked an AI provider yet.
stage.noProvider.instructions: Open Settings → Knowledge Base, choose a provider (free local model recommended for first-time users), paste the API key if it needs one, and save. It takes effect immediately — no restart needed.

tutorial.bullet.context: Surfaces relevant context the moment you need it.

tutorial.advanced.hint: Point the desktop client at a GBrain instance you've started yourself (custom port, remote server, etc).
oneClick.title: Enable Knowledge Base
oneClick.description: Let the assistant install and start GBrain for you — no terminal commands required.
